title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 4° of the notes. It sets up the identification of the Z-extension of GL(2,Z) constructed in 3° with the 'S'-extension of the mapping class group T_{1,1}.

(35) X_1 = R^2/Z^2 = (R/Z)^2 = U×U is the standard genus-1 surface, written additively.

(36) The marked point is a_{1,0} = 0. U_{1,1} = X_1 minus {0} is the standard once-punctured torus, of type (g,ν) = (1,1).

GL(2,Z) is the automorphism group of the topological group X_1. It therefore acts on X_1 fixing 0, hence acts on U_{1,1}. This gives a homomorphism (37) GL(2,Z) → T_{1,1} = T(U_{1,1}), the group of isotopy classes of homeomorphisms. Orientation-reversing classes are included, so this is the extended mapping class group. The homomorphism is classically an isomorphism.

The action is moreover differentiable. The induced action on the tangent space at 0 is the tautological action of GL(2,Z) ⊂ GL(2,R) on R^2. So the Z-extension G~ defined in 3° is a pullback along a homomorphism to GL(2,R): the one induced by π_1(GL^+(2,R)) = Z, i.e. by rotation of tangent directions at the fixed point (in the GL case Z is acted on by orientation sign). This G~ is to be compared with the extension S T_{1,1}: mapping classes together with the tangential/boundary datum at the puncture, i.e. the mapping class group of the torus with one boundary component.

The next page concludes the theorem. The pullback of S T_{1,1} via (37) is canonically GL(2,Z)~, with two explicit presentations:
- ρ^3 σ^{-2} = 1 plus an involution τ' inverting ρ and σ;
- three involutions r_0, r_1, r_∞ with (r_0 r_1)^3 (r_∞ r_0)^2 = 1.

The orientation-preserving part is the classical B_3 ≅ Mod(Σ_1^1) ≅ the preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R). The section then turns to describing T_{1,1} via Autext of π_1(U_{1,1}).
errors: 'il opère sur U_{1,0}' should read U_{1,1} (slip or misreading).
Minor: for orientation-reversing elements the Z-extension is not central (Z is acted on by the sign). Grothendieck handles this in 3°, so it is not a real gap.

ideas.what: GL(2,Z) ≅ extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus, via linear automorphisms of R^2/Z^2
ideas.where_published: Context of La Longue Marche (1981, circulated); not as such in Esquisse

ideas.what: The central/Z-extension of the mapping class group obtained via the tangent action at the fixed point, identified with the pullback of the universal cover of GL(2,R)
ideas.modern_name: Mod(Σ_1^1) ≅ B_3 ≅ preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R) (here extended to GL)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Artin braid group B_3; Milnor; Birman)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (circulated manuscript)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but classical identification of GL(2,Z) and its Z-extension with the (tangentially framed) mapping class group of the one-punctured torus. The presentation via three involutions for the GL version is a mild variant of the known B_3 picture, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The title appears to read 'GL(2,Z)^~ ≃ S T_{1,1}': the S looks overwritten or emphasised rather than clearly deleted, which is consistent with the theorem on the next page.
'U_{1,0}' in the image is a slip for U_{1,1}.
'd'où un homo' continues as 'homomorphisme' (37), written with a ~ over the arrow.
On the next page 'MB.' is likely 'NB.'
